title: Operation Epic Fury: 6,000 targets, 90 Iranian vessels hit, claims US
byline: The United States has struck about 6,000 targets in Iran and damaged or destroyed more than 90 Iranian vessels, including over 60 ships and at least 30 minelayers, as part of the ongoing Operation Epic Fury, according to an official U.S. military fact sheet released on Wednesday.

title: US allows countries to buy Russian oil stranded at sea for 30 days
byline: The United States issued a 30-day license for countries to buy Russian oil and petroleum products currently stranded at sea in what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said was a step to stabilize global energy markets roiled by the Iran war.

title: US carrying out rescue effort after military aircraft crash in Iraq
byline: A U.S. military refueling aircraft crashed in western Iraq on Thursday, in an incident U.S. Central Command said involved another aircraft but was not the result of hostile or friendly fire.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa and Northwestern provinces and in Galle, Matara, Kandy and Nuwara-Eliya districts after 2.00 pm today (13), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Netanyahu threatens Iran new leader, says government collapse uncertain
byline: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday issued a veiled threat to kill Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei even as he acknowledged that Israel’s joint air war with the U.S. may not lead to a collapse of Tehran’s clerical government.

title: Trump issues new threat to Iran’s leaders, calling them ‘deranged scumbags’
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a new threat online to Iran, writing: “Watch what happens to these deranged scumbags today.”

title: Rapper-politician Balendra Shah’s party wins Nepal election
byline: The Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) has won a landslide in Nepal’s election - the first held since last year’s youth-led protests toppled the then government.

title: Public urged to be vigilant over online ads during festive period – CERT
byline: The Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (SL CERT) has issued a public advisory urging people to exercise caution when engaging with online advertisements as the festive season approaches.

title: Iran-backed Iraqi group claims responsibility for downing US military aircraft
byline: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella group of Iran-backed armed factions, claimed ⁠responsibility for downing a U.S. military refueling aircraft in western Iraq on Thursday.

title: Over 650kg of Ice & heroin, seized from fishing vessel escorted to Dikkovita Harbour
byline: A total of 654 kilograms of narcotics, comprising 478 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine (ICE) and 176 kilograms of heroin, were recovered from the multi-day fishing vessel that was escorted by the Sri Lanka Navy to the Dikkovita Fisheries Harbour yesterday, said police.

title: Netflix announces KPop Demon Hunters sequel
byline: Netflix has announced a sequel to KPop Demon Hunters, the streaming platform’s most watched movie of all time.

title: One-fifth of Australian teens still use TikTok, SnapChat after social media ban
byline: One-fifth of Australian teenagers under 16 were still using social media two months after the country banned platforms from allowing minors, industry data showed, raising questions about the effectiveness of age-gating methods they are using.

title: Corruption probe against Shasheendra Rajapaksa concluded: Bribery Comm. informs court
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) informed the Colombo Magistrate’s Court today that investigations into former State Minister Shasheendra Rajapaksa and other suspects, who are currently out on bail in connection with a corruption allegation, have been concluded.

title: Low-floor buses for persons with disabilities to be deployed from April
byline: Additional Secretary to the President (Clean Sri Lanka Programme), Engineer S.P.C. Sugeeshwara, stated that plans are underway to deploy the low-floor buses, imported for the benefit of persons with disabilities, ahead of the upcoming Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: 84 Iranian sailors’ remains to be repatriated on special flight today – Defence Ministry
byline: The bodies of 84 Iranian sailors killed in the torpedo attack on the warship IRIS Dena off Sri Lanka’s coast are scheduled to be repatriated to Iran today on a special flight departing from Mattala International Airport, the Defence Ministry said.

title: ‘Watch what happens’: Trump issues new threat to Iran
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a new threat online to Iran, writing: “Watch what happens to these deranged scumbags today.”

title: Compensation process begins for farmers affected by crop damage in 2025/26 ‘Maha Season’
byline: The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board has announced that damage assessment activities have already commenced in the relevant districts for the release of compensation to farmers affected by crop damage during the 2025/2026 ‘Maha season’.

title: Sri Lanka’s largest groundwater source discovered in Pitabeddara
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) says it has discovered the largest groundwater source in Sri Lanka thus far during tube well drilling carried out near the Pitabeddara Police Station.

title: Sri Lanka’s Foreign Minister begins talks to purchase fuel from Russia
byline: A meeting was held between the Russian Ambassador to Sri Lanka, Levan S. Dzhagaryan, and Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism this afternoon (13).

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and Galle and Matara districts.

title: Low-floor buses for persons with disabilities to be deployed before Sinhala and Tamil New Year
byline: Additional Secretary to the President (Clean Sri Lanka Programme), Engineer S.P.C. Sugeeshwara, stated that plans are underway to deploy the low-floor buses, imported for the benefit of persons with disabilities, ahead of the upcoming Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Police destroy nearly 200kg of seized narcotics related to concluded cases
byline: Nearly 200 kilograms of seized narcotics related to concluded cases were destroyed by Sri Lanka today (13) at the incinerator located at Lactowatte, Wanathawilluwa.

title: At least 1,444 killed by US-Israeli attacks on Iran
byline: At least 1,444 people have been killed and 18,551 injured by US-Israeli attacks on Iran since February 28, Iran’s Health Ministry says.

title: Four killed after US refuelling plane crashes in Iraq, military confirms
byline: Four of six crew aboard a US military refuelling aircraft have died after it crashed in western Iraq, US Central Command (Centcom) says.

title: One-fourth of Sri Lanka’s population living in poverty - Minister Upali Pannilage
byline: According to the Ministry of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment, one-fourth of Sri Lanka’s population is currently living in poverty.

title: Easter attacks case against Hemasiri and Pujith taken up in court
byline: The Colombo Special High Court Trial-at-Bar has ordered to present defence evidence on March 26 related to the case filed against former Defence Secretary Hemasiri Fernando and former Inspector General of Police Pujith Jayasundara.

title: Sri Lanka’s language diversity reflects richness of pluralistic heritage – PM Harini
byline: Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya participated as the Chief Guest in the special event organized to commentate the International Mother Language Day 2026 on Friday (13) at the New Arts Theatre of the University of Colombo.

title: Iranian state television reports large explosion in Tehran near protests
byline: Iranian state television reports a large explosion in a Tehran square where demonstrations were supposed to be happening.

title: Electricity trade unions hail ‘successful’ talks with the President
byline: The electricity-sector trade unions, who met with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake this afternoon (13) to discuss their issues, say that the talks were successful.

title: Iran’s new supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei wounded, likely disfigured: Hegseth
byline: Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is wounded and likely disfigured, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday (Mar 13), questioning Khamenei’s ability to govern after nearly two weeks of US and Israeli attacks on Iran.

title: S. Satheestharan appointed as High Court Judge
byline: Former District Judge of Chavakachcheri, Mr S. Satheestharan, has been appointed as a High Court Judge, the President’s Media Division said.

title: Rubies worth Rs. 6 million stolen from gem merchant in Kandy
byline: An individual has stolen a box containing several rubies from a gem merchant at E.L. Senanayake Veediya in Kandy this afternoon (13).

title: Committee on Economic Surveillance discusses urgent measures to stabilise domestic market
byline: The Committee on Economic Surveillance, established to safeguard Sri Lanka’s economic stability and protect the welfare of citizens amid external pressures, has met at the Presidential Secretariat under the chairmanship of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: All six crew members killed in US refuelling plane crash
byline: All six crew members have been killed in the crash of a refuelling plane in Iraq, the US Central Command has said.

title: ‘No-one will hire women’ - India’s top court rejects menstrual leave petition
byline: India’s top court has rejected a petition seeking menstrual leave for working women and female students with the judges saying if they were to make such a law, “no-one will hire women”.

title: Promoting local industry a key government priority - PM Harini
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya stated that promoting the local industrial sector is one of the key priorities of the Government.

title: President assures protection of CEB employees’ rights amid restructuring
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake stated that the government is committed to addressing all issues faced by employees of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) at the earliest possible opportunity.
